title: Seniority, security, and recovery
objectives: Answer out loud: What's the absolute priority rule?
Answer out loud: What's structural subordination?

steps.body: **Secured** debt is backed by specific collateral; **unsecured** relies on the general claim.
In bankruptcy, the **absolute priority rule** says senior claims are paid in full before junior claims get anything.
Order: secured debt → senior unsecured → subordinated → preferred → common equity.

blocks.title: What's structural subordination?
blocks.teaser: Debt at a holding company is effectively junior to debt at its operating subsidiaries, because the subsidiaries' creditors get paid from the subsidia…
blocks.body:
Debt at a holding company is effectively junior to debt at its operating subsidiaries, because the subsidiaries' creditors get paid from the subsidiaries' assets before any value flows up to the holdco.

**Interview answer:** "Holdco debt only gets what's left after opco creditors are paid, so it's effectively junior even if it's labeled senior."

blocks.prompt: Senior notes are issued at the holding company; term loans sit at the operating subsidiary. Who is effectively senior?

options.text: The holdco senior notes, because they're labeled senior
The opco term loans, because they're paid from the subsidiary's assets first

blocks.explanation: Structural subordination: holdco creditors only get what flows up after opco creditors are paid, even if labeled "senior."

blocks.title: Chapter 11 vs. Chapter 7?
blocks.teaser: Chapter 11 is a reorganization: the company keeps operating while restructuring debt (often converting debt to equity).
blocks.body: Chapter 11 is a reorganization: the company keeps operating while restructuring debt (often converting debt to equity). Chapter 7 is liquidation: assets are sold and proceeds distributed by priority.

blocks.title: What's DIP financing?
blocks.teaser: Debtor-in-possession financing — new loans to a company in Chapter 11.
blocks.body: Debtor-in-possession financing — new loans to a company in Chapter 11. It gets super-priority over existing debt so lenders are willing to fund a bankrupt company.

blocks.title: Why does recovery vary by tranche?
blocks.teaser: Senior secured lenders often recover most or all of their principal; unsecured and subordinated holders recover far less; equity is often wiped out.
blocks.body: Senior secured lenders often recover most or all of their principal; unsecured and subordinated holders recover far less; equity is often wiped out.
